questions.scenario: Untrusted pull-request code runs on a persistent worker later reused by a privileged release job. Reviewers see no secrets in the PR job's environment and conclude the arrangement is safe. What is the missing concern?

options.text: A different job name automatically resets the host and removes the concern.
Untrusted work can contaminate persistent worker state later consumed by privileged work.
Only the repository branch name determines whether the worker remains trustworthy.
Removing log output prevents all cross-job effects from untrusted execution.

questions.explanation: The worker itself is a trust boundary. Persistent compromise can survive job boundaries even without secrets in the first job. Labels, branch names, and quieter logs do not establish isolation or cleanup. [Official reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use).

questions.scenario: A package's digest matches a registry entry and its checksum verifies. The team has no accepted statement connecting that package to its reviewed repository and approved builder. Which conclusion is justified?

options.text: The checksum proves the package contains only reviewed source.
The registry entry proves the publishing identity was authorized.
The package must be safe because corruption was not detected.
Integrity is established against that digest, but trusted build provenance is still missing.

questions.explanation: A matching digest identifies bytes; it does not identify an authorized producer or prove a reviewed build path. Provenance and its verification supply different evidence from a checksum. [Official reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/secure-your-work/use-artifact-attestations/use-artifact-attestations).

questions.scenario: A job can execute contributor-controlled code while holding a production credential. The CI platform masks recognized secret values in displayed logs. Is that enough to protect the credential?

options.text: No; restrict credential access and untrusted execution because log masking is only one defense.
Yes; masked log output removes the credential from the process environment.
Yes; a contributor cannot use a value that reviewers cannot read in the UI.
No; the only useful change is making the logs completely private.

questions.explanation: Masking affects log presentation, not arbitrary code's authority to use or transmit a credential. Isolation and least privilege address that boundary; private logs alone do not prevent misuse. [Official reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/security/secure-use).

questions.scenario: A release requires a passing security report for its exact artifact. The scanner service is unavailable, and the workflow receives no report. Someone suggests treating the absence of findings as a pass. Which policy matches the requirement?

options.text: Pass because an unavailable report contains zero reported findings.
Reuse any older report that has the same application name.
Block promotion and recover the required evidence or use an explicitly authorized exception process.
Allow deployment now and make the next release wait for two reports.

questions.explanation: Missing evidence is not a passing decision. The stated gate requires current artifact-bound evidence or a separately authorized exception. Names, deferred promises, and counting absent findings do not satisfy it. [Official reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/reference/workflows-and-actions/deployments-and-environments).

questions.scenario: A release review has an SBOM, a package digest, and a signed provenance statement from an approved build identity. Which two interpretations correctly distinguish these records?

options.text: The SBOM describes components and can help locate affected releases when a vulnerability is disclosed.
The SBOM alone proves the runtime cannot contain an exploitable vulnerability.
The verified provenance connects the identified artifact to claims about its build origin.
A valid signature makes functional checks and release policy unnecessary.

questions.explanation: Inventory and provenance answer different questions: what components are recorded and where the artifact came from. Neither establishes functional correctness or freedom from vulnerabilities, and signing does not replace release policy. [Official reference](https://docs.github.com/en/actions/how-tos/secure-your-work/use-artifact-attestations/use-artifact-attestations).
